mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases > 5% YoY and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting corporate margins and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines > 2% YoY and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) coupled with a decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals strong consumer demand and confidence, boosting corporate revenues and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 5% YoY and UNRATE decreases > 0.5pp
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases > 5% YoY and UNRATE decreases > 0.5pp, but S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals accommodative monetary policy, which encourages risk-taking and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.5pp, but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) above 3% YoY signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 increases > 3% YoY and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis fails.
